rewrites.summary: The controlling risk for a transgender visitor is judicial: in early October 2023 the Court of Appeals of Iquique annulled a femicide conviction in whole, holding that the offence covers only 'a person biologically female' — the strongest gendered-violence protection in the penal code therefore does not extend to trans women in Tarapacá. The region's 1.56 % share of nationally documented anti-LGBTI cases is small but rising (+18.18 % year-on-year), so a trans visitor faces a documented protection gap against gender-motivated violence rather than high absolute case volume.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: Comparison context rather than local risk: the region sits at −0.08 against the national 0.72, it is 0.01 below the compared region La Araucanía (0.65), whose −0.07 is trend-based (+150 % rise, low visibility) rather than ruling-based, and 0.05 below the other compared region Arica y Parinacota (0.69), whose deviation rests on the shared northern-court context with no trans-specific incident of its own. The national framework (Law 21.120 and the femicide article) is unchanged, so the flux is judicial-interpretive rather than legislative.
rewrites.localsOnly: The killing that produced the finding is a resident-facing case fact: a 55-year-old trans woman whose body was found on the southern coast of the provincial capital in June 2022; her killer was convicted at first instance to presidio perpetuo, and on the defence's nullity motion the Iquique court declared the sentence void in early October 2023.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes: The case-share figures (1.56 % of the national total; +18.18 % year-on-year) rest on the annual-report dataset, which no region-specific source independently covers. No source documents border-screening practice, documents handling, or marriage/partner-travel matters for transgender visitors in this region, so the visitor assessment rests on the judicial finding and the case-share signal alone.

blindSourceSummaries: An October 2023 news report: the appeals court annulled the trial of a man convicted for the 2022 murder of a trans woman, holding that the 'femicide' offence covers only 'a person biologically female' and so the conviction could not stand as framed — voiding the strongest gendered-violence conviction available; the ruling was delivered in the state/province, where that court exercises jurisdiction.

The 2024 annual human-rights report on sexual and gender diversity (published March 2025, 2024 data): the state/province held about two per cent of the nationally documented homo/transphobic cases and ranked among the fastest-rising regions (+18.18 % year-on-year, with growth also flagged at +19.51 % in the period tables) — the dataset basis of the record's case-share claim, which no region-specific source covers.
rewrites.notes: Split from merged summary per rule 6: judicial protection-gap finding and case-share practical context to summary; score comparisons and the unchanged national framework to tangentialFactors; resident case facts to localsOnly. Blind mirrors genericised per rule 7/7e: court name, region name, victim/defendant names, age, coastal location, and law number (Law 21.120) dropped as identity-granular; 'state/province' used as the unit placeholder; dates of the ruling and report kept.
